title: All Saints
subtitle: Solemnity (replaces the 31st Sunday in Ordinary Time) · Rev 7:2-4, 9-14; 1 Jn 3:1-3; Mt 5:1-12a
text: Today the Church honors the whole company of heaven, a great multitude no one could count, from every nation, race, people, and tongue. Most of them never got a feast day of their own: mothers, farmers, soldiers, children, ordinary people who lived the Beatitudes. "Beloved, we are God's children now; what we shall be has not yet been revealed."
imageAlt: Dürer's altarpiece showing the Holy Trinity above, with the crucified Christ held by God the Father beneath the dove of the Holy Spirit, surrounded by tiers of saints, angels, popes, emperors, and ordinary men and women in adoration, above a small landscape.
credit: Albrecht Dürer, Adoration of the Trinity (Landauer Altar), 1511, Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (Google Art Project)
